editorial.assessment: Church Presenter is a recently published free open-source option with an unusually broad stated feature set. Its appeal is clear for budget-limited teams, but churches should check platform support and training, assess project maturity and test real-service reliability before moving away from an established presenter.

longForm.verdict: Church Presenter looks promising for teams that want a no-subscription, offline-capable worship tool across common desktop platforms. Its relative newness means a staged rehearsal and fallback plan are important before a live migration.

decisionLens.heading: Treat the first live services as a controlled rollout.
decisionLens.text: Free and cross-platform does not automatically mean every church’s files, displays and volunteers will behave consistently. Test the ordinary service order, presentations, lyrics, Bible lookups and remote control, then keep the previous system ready until confidence is established.

sections.heading: A free cross-platform worship tool
sections.question: Can it meet the church’s full service workflow?
paragraphs: Church Presenter describes Bible and song presentation, video, imported slideshows, announcements, service-order planning, multi-screen output and mobile remote control. It says it runs on Windows, macOS and Linux and is free under GNU GPL v3.

Run a rehearsal with the actual output hardware and a licensed service plan. Keep responsibility for CCLI reporting, Bible rights and streaming permissions separate from the software choice, because no free tool supplies those permissions automatically.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use an independent review score. It is based on Church Presenter’s official product, licensing and release material.
themes: Free licensing lowers the cost of a realistic team trial.
A newly released project needs a cautious live-service rollout and fallback.
userFeedback.caveat: Supplier claims are not independent testing, and open-source availability does not establish production readiness for a particular church.

faq.question: Is Church Presenter free?
faq.answer: Yes. Church Presenter says it is GNU GPL v3, free forever, with no subscription or seat limits.

faq.question: Does Church Presenter offer a trial?
faq.answer: No trial is needed because the software is free to download and use.

faq.question: Which systems does Church Presenter run on?
faq.answer: The supplier says it runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, with mobile apps for remote control.

faq.question: Does Church Presenter include music licences?
faq.answer: Churches remain responsible for CCLI and other content or streaming licences.
